summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, heart failure, and a history of stroke, presented with hypotension during dialysis. Upon arrival, he expressed a strong desire to leave the hospital and was assessed as having decision-making capacity. He refused physical examination but consented to a chest X-ray and blood cultures. Imaging showed no acute cardiopulmonary issues and stable positioning of his dialysis catheter. Blood cultures showed no growth, suggesting no active bloodstream infection. After discussion of risks, he chose to be discharged against medical advice. He was counseled on warning signs and the importance of follow-up with his nephrologist. The hospital course was brief and non-interventional.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 5 chronic kidney disease or end stage renal disease
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Anemia in other chronic diseases classified elsewhere
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Hemiplegia and hemiparesis following cerebral infarction affecting right dominant side
